yarn-dinkum.meaning: All facts kept: 28 years at the Bureau, pneumonia at 73, the "reform fanatic" charge, prohibition and narcotics laws, Sunday amusements, the Dempsey-Carpentier bout, Westerly burial, the career moves, Sara J. Timanus, six lectures a week, "Rhetoric Made Racy", the Quarterly, the list of targets. "durries" renders cigarettes.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "gave him a fair whack of the credit", "had a red-hot go at stopping the Dempsey-Carpentier bout", "sheer hard yakka", "wrote a stack on moral questions", "durries".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural Aussie mostly ("fair whack", "hard yakka", "precious little rest", "durries"), with one American form: "The folks on the other side".
yarn-dinkum.register: Close to level 4: most sentences are retold ("He never minced words", "a red-hot go", "a fair whack of the credit") while the obituary frame stays. No swearing, within vulgarity 1.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the sober obituary with its dry irony about the reformer's targets: "those were just a few of the things his tireless reforming zeal took aim at."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads well, with one clumsy join that names him after a pronoun: "He never minced words about Sunday amusements, and Dr. Crafts tried to have them banned by law."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "had him down as", "fair whack", "rein in", "never minced words", "red-hot go", "a stack", "hard yakka", "pops up", "raise an eyebrow", "durries".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the 1922 obituary, its shape and its wry closing catalogue intact: "Screen vampires, close dancing, "joy rides,"".

dinkum-4.meaning: All facts kept, in the original order: "whose opponents had him pegged as a "reform fanatic"", "He averaged six lectures a week, given in twenty-nine different countries", "since 1896".
dinkum-4.sense: Terms fit: "had him pegged as", "Those who were on side with his policies", "barely got a spell", "wrote heaps", "ciggies".
dinkum-4.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian writing: "on side", "barely got a spell", "sheer hard yakka", "ciggies"; nothing stock or foreign.
dinkum-4.register: Lighter than level 4: a light-to-middle touch with much near the original ("He graduated from Wesleyan in 1869 and from the Divinity School of Boston University in 1871."). No swearing.
dinkum-4.tone: The obituary's sobriety and dry irony survive: "those were a few of the targets of his tireless reforming zeal."
dinkum-4.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Never one to keep quiet about his dislike of Sunday amusements, Dr. Crafts tried to have them banned by law."
dinkum-4.variety: Varied though sparer: "pegged", "on side", "had a go", "heaps", "hard yakka", "a spell", "ciggies".
dinkum-4.essence: Clearly the original obituary, retold: "Here, for instance, is an odd title that crops up".

dinkum-3.meaning: All facts kept, with the lead restructured: "Dr. Wilbur F. Crafts has died of pneumonia in hospital here today, aged 73." "well known right across the country" slightly narrows "widely known". Nothing invented.
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "The mob on the other side of the laws he pushed", "reckoned he'd had a big hand", "stayed put", "ciggies".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural but thin: "The mob on the other side", "in hospital", "stayed put", "ciggies"; most of the text is plain Australian-neutral English.
dinkum-3.register: Lighter than level 4: "there can't have been many who got through as much work as Dr. Crafts did" and "His pen and his voice barely got a rest" are plain paraphrase rather than Aussie. No swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the sober obituary and its irony: "those were just a few of the things his tireless reforming zeal took on."
dinkum-3.flow: Mostly smooth; one twisted sentence: "In a long list of titles that won't surprise anyone, for instance, there's this odd one that crops up: "Rhetoric Made Racy.""
dinkum-3.variety: Few Aussie terms, and "a go" style phrasing repeats in spirit: "did his best", "a fair bit", "having a go at popular amusements"; little range.
dinkum-3.essence: Recognisably the original obituary with its closing catalogue: "Screen vampires, close dancing, "joy rides,"".

yarn-dinkum.quote: The folks on the other side
yarn-dinkum.why: "folks" is American; an Australian would say mob or people.

yarn-dinkum.quote: He never minced words about Sunday amusements, and Dr. Crafts tried
yarn-dinkum.original: Outspoken in his opposition to Sunday amusements, Dr. Crafts sought
yarn-dinkum.why: Pronoun then full name in the same sentence reads clumsily.

dinkum-4.quote: He graduated from Wesleyan in 1869 and from the Divinity School of Boston University in 1871.
dinkum-4.original: He was graduated from Wesleyan in 1869 and from the Divinity School of Boston University in 1871.
dinkum-4.why: Long stretches left nearly as in the original; lighter than the level-4 brief.

dinkum-3.quote: there can't have been many who got through as much work as Dr. Crafts did
dinkum-3.original: few can have equaled Dr. Crafts in the amount of work done
dinkum-3.why: Plain paraphrase where the brief calls for level-4 Aussie; typical of the whole text.

dinkum-3.quote: In a long list of titles that won't surprise anyone, for instance, there's this odd one that crops up
dinkum-3.original: Here, for instance, is a curious title that crops up in a long list of others that do not surprise

summaries.yarn-dinkum: The fullest Aussie retelling, near the level-4 brief, faithful and varied, with a US "folks" and one clumsy join.
summaries.dinkum-4: The most natural and smoothest of the three, faithful throughout, but lighter than level 4.
summaries.dinkum-3: Faithful and natural, but the lightest and least varied retelling, well under level 4.
